turn/pair: Draw a pair of numbers as an arrow from the origin. Here is a query, q: two, one.
turn/turn: Rotating turns the arrow about the origin, keeping its length: a quarter turn, ninety degrees, carries it to minus one, two.
turn/unit: To turn any pair, start from an arrow of length one, pointing right, and turn it by the angle. Its tip lands at two numbers: across, the angle's cosine, written cos, and up, its sine, written sine.
turn/cossin: At ninety degrees the arrow points straight up: cos is zero and sin is one. At sixty degrees it lands one half across and about zero point eight seven up. Like e to a power, they are looked up, not worked out by hand.
turn/basis: So one, zero turns to cos, sin. And zero, one is one, zero already turned a quarter, so it lands a quarter turn past cos, sin. A quarter turn swaps the entries and flips the first sign, as two, one became minus one, two: minus sin, cos.
turn/rule: Any pair a, b is a times one, zero, plus b times zero, one. Turning moves both pieces, so it lands at a times cos, sin, plus b times minus sin, cos: a cos minus b sin, and a sin plus b cos.
turn/check: For ninety degrees: two times zero minus one times one is minus one, and two times one plus one times zero is two.
turn/sixty: At sixty degrees, with cosine one half and sine about zero point eight seven, the key one, one turns to about minus zero point three seven and one point three seven.
position/idea: Rotary positions mark where a token sits by turning each query and key, instead of adding a position vector.
position/angle: Each pair turns by a fixed angle per position, written theta, the Greek letter theta. At position m, it has turned by m times theta.
position/example: With theta of thirty degrees, position zero is not turned, and position three turns by ninety.
position/pairs: A query of d k entries makes d k over two pairs, each with its own theta, some fast and some slow.
position/only: Nothing is learned or added to the token: only queries and keys turn, just before scoring.
relative/both: Turn a query and a key by the same angle, and they move together: their dot product stays the same.
relative/numbers: Two, one dotted with one, one is three. Turned ninety degrees each, they still give three.
relative/apart: Now a query at position five turns by five theta, and a key at position two by two theta.
relative/shift: Move both four places later, to nine and six. Each turns four theta more, together, so the score stays the same.
relative/distance: So the score depends only on how far apart the tokens are, and which comes first.
relative/try: Try one, with theta of ninety degrees: the query two, one at position one, and the key one, one at position zero.
relative/tq: The query turns by one times ninety degrees: two times zero minus one times one is minus one, and two times one plus one times zero is two. The key, at position zero, does not turn.
relative/tdot: Dot them: minus one times one, plus two times one. The score is one, where the unturned pair gave three.
